newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr firms vs yen, down vs mark on French election.
newsitem.headline: Dlr firms vs yen, down vs mark on French election.

text.p: *Dollar well-bid against yen in early trade partly due to talk of bids from Japanese public investors below 115.50 yen and mark purchases against yen, dealers said.
*There was talk that government-related bodies were placing bids at 115.50 yen and below, said a Japanese bank trader.
*"I think the (Japanese) government does not want to see the dollar falling below 112 yen," he added.
*Dollar fell against German mark in early Asian trade after left-wing parties took unexpectedly strong lead in first round of French elections on Sunday, dealers said.

*Dealers said there would be uncertainty about French politics until after June 1 second round, but doubts over Socialists' stance on European Monetary Union have pushed French franc down against the mark and lifted mark vs dollar.
*"The outcome of (the French election) was out of line with expectations," said dealer at a trust bank said.
*Mark expected to strengthen against U.S. dollar and French franc due to uncertainty about French election.
*"The market's focus is likely to shift from dollar/yen to dollar/European currencies," the first dealer said.

*Before first-round projections came in from 1800 GMT, franc had been trading at 3.712/3.716 against the German mark. After results it slipped to 3.720/25 and was standing at 3.3745/50 against mark at 0332 GMT.

*Senior Japanese Finance Ministry official Eisuke Sakakibara was quoted as telling Le Monde that a rise in Japan's discount rate to 1.0 percent is expected in the coming year. But the dollar has not reacted much to this report.
